correctness.rationale: For a nonempty finite base A, B=dcl(A) is a finite meet-closed rooted tree of size s. QE and homogeneous finite meet-tree embeddings reduce S_1(A) to distinct one-point generated meet-tree extensions over B. The standard one-point lemma permits only the new realization x and possibly the maximal meet y=max{x meet b:b in B}. The s realized x=b types, 1+(s-1)=s linear-gap insertion types, s types in a fresh cone above an old vertex, and s new-meet branching types in the same s gaps are exhaustive and pairwise distinct: total 4s. Every extension is realized by density/infinite cone branching. In the meet-closure of m generators every unmarked/new vertex has >=2 children, giving s<=2m-1, and chains/full binary leaf sets attain s=m and s=2m-1. The m=1 and A=empty boundary cases are handled separately. Independent fresh rooted-tree enumeration (not a proof of the infinite assertion) checked all labeled B for s=1,2,3 with (no_extra,extra)=(2s,s). The claimed finite verifier was inspected but not treated as a proof or blindly rerun.
